words.ex: It would be premature to declare the translation industry dead simply because machine output has improved.
The software produced a usable draft, albeit one riddled with subtle errors of register.
In all likelihood, translators will become editors of machine output rather than disappear altogether.
I can only offer a tentative answer, since the technology is evolving faster than the research.
She argued with real conviction that poetry can never be fully automated.
You could make a case for AI in legal translation, where consistency matters more than style.

dialogue.t: So, do you reckon AI will put human translators out of work within the next decade?
It would be premature to suggest that the profession is doomed. Machines still stumble over idioms, humour and cultural references.
Granted, but there's a strong case to be made that routine work, like product manuals and contracts, is already being automated.
That's fair. I'm inclined to think the routine end of the market will shrink, albeit with reservations about how quickly it'll happen.
What about literary translation? Translating Mahmoud Darwish into English, for instance?
There, I'm far more confident. In all likelihood, readers will always want a human sensibility behind a poem.
So your position is that the job will change rather than vanish?
Precisely. I'd stop short of saying it's guaranteed, but that's where the evidence seems to point.

grammar.title: Graded Modality and Hedging
grammar.ar: في المستوى المتقدّم لا يكفي أن تقول رأيك، بل عليك أن تُبيّن درجة يقينك به بدقة. نستخدم عبارات مثل It would be premature to suggest that للتعبير عن الحذر الشديد، وI'm inclined to think للميل الشخصي غير القاطع، وIn all likelihood وThere is a strong case to be made that للترجيح القوي. ويختلف هذا عن العربية التي تميل أحيانًا إلى الجزم أو المبالغة في التوكيد، فاستخدام التحوّط في الإنجليزية الأكاديمية يدلّ على النضج الفكري لا على الضعف.
examples: It would be premature to suggest that machine translation has matched human accuracy.
I'm inclined to think that bilingual editors will be in demand, albeit with reservations about pay.
In all likelihood, the most creative forms of translation will remain human for decades.

words.ex: When my father said the car was 'nearly empty', he was implying that I should fill it up.
From her silence, I inferred that she wasn't happy with the arrangement.
The subtext of the manager's email was clear: nobody should leave early on Thursday.
His comment about my 'ambitious' timetable was a veiled criticism.
She gave a tactful reply that acknowledged his effort without praising the result.
If you read between the lines, the school is really saying the trip might be cancelled.

dialogue.t: My teacher looked at my essay plan and just said, 'Well, that's certainly an interesting angle.' What do you make of that?
Hmm. What she seems to be implying is that the angle is a bit risky, maybe even off-topic.
That's what I was afraid of. And then she added, 'You might want to look at the rubric again.'
Reading between the lines, she thinks you haven't fully answered the question. That's not to say that your idea is bad, though.
So should I scrap it completely?
Not necessarily. You could ask her directly, but tactfully. Something like, 'I take it you're not entirely convinced by my approach?'
That sounds less defensive than asking, 'Don't you like it?'
Exactly. It shows you've picked up on the hint and invites her to be more specific.

grammar.title: Voicing Implicature
grammar.ar: المعنى الضمني (implicature) هو ما يقصده المتكلّم دون أن يصرّح به. نستخدم What she seems to be implying is أو Reading between the lines لنُفصح عن هذا المعنى بأدب، ونستخدم سؤالًا بصيغة الخبر مثل I take it you're not entirely convinced? لنتحقّق من استنتاجنا دون اتهام. أما That's not to say that فتمنع الطرف الآخر من فهم كلامنا بشكل مبالغ فيه.
examples: What he seems to be implying is that we should have consulted him first.
I take it you'd rather we postponed the meeting?
The feedback was critical. That's not to say that the project was a failure, however.

words.ar: التهوين / التقليل المتعمَّد من شأن الشيء
words.ex: Calling the traffic 'a bit slow' was an understatement; we didn't move for an hour.
Sarcasm rarely translates well in text messages, because the reader can't hear your tone.
His review of the restaurant was entirely tongue-in-cheek, but some readers took it literally.
She delivered the joke in such a deadpan voice that half the class didn't realise she was joking.
The organisers' response to the complaints was disappointing, to say the least.
The brand's attempt at humour backfired when customers found the post insensitive.

dialogue.t: Have you seen that viral post from the influencer who 'surprised' her followers with a launch event in the middle of a sandstorm?
I have. It wasn't exactly a triumph, was it? Half the guests left before she even arrived.
That's putting it mildly. Someone commented, 'Great planning, as always!' with a dozen clapping emojis.
Pure sarcasm. One might be forgiven for thinking it was praise, though, if you only read the words.
And then her manager replied, 'Well, the weather wasn't on our side.' Not the most tactful remark, to say the least.
Especially since the forecast had warned about the storm for days. Blaming the weather really backfired.
It's fascinating how the same sentence can sound sincere or mocking depending on the context.
Absolutely. Online, tone is carried by emojis, punctuation and shared knowledge rather than by voice.

grammar.title: Understatement and Ironic Framing
grammar.ar: يميل المتحدّثون بالإنجليزية، وخاصة البريطانيون، إلى التعبير عن الانتقاد أو الدهشة بالتهوين بدل المبالغة، مثل استخدام النفي في It wasn't exactly a triumph بمعنى أنه كان فشلًا. وتستخدم One might be forgiven for thinking لإظهار أن الانطباع الظاهر مضلِّل، بينما تؤكّد That's putting it mildly وto say the least أن الحقيقة أسوأ مما قيل. فهم هذه الأساليب ضروري لأن المعنى الحقيقي غالبًا عكس المعنى الحرفي.
examples: His speech wasn't exactly inspiring; several people were checking their phones.
One might be forgiven for thinking the company had apologised, but the statement admits nothing.
The final exam was challenging, and that's putting it mildly.

words.ar: في غاية الحيرة والإرهاق / لم يعُد يعرف ما يفعل
words.ex: By Wednesday night I was at my wits' end, with three exams and no idea where to start.
Getting lost turned out to be a blessing in disguise, because we found the most beautiful dunes.

words.ar: يكتفي بـ / يتدبّر أمره بما هو متاح
words.ex: We forgot the gas cylinder, so we had to make do with a campfire.
It finally dawned on me that I'd been revising the wrong chapter.
I pulled an all-nighter before chemistry and regretted it the moment I saw the first question.

words.ar: يُنهي السهرة / يكتفي بهذا القدر لليوم
words.ex: Around two in the morning, we put out the fire and called it a night.

dialogue.t: So how was the camping trip? You look like you haven't slept in a week.
Honestly, it started as a disaster. Our 4x4 got stuck in the sand an hour after we left the main road.
No way! What did you do?
We tried everything. By sunset, I was at my wits' end. We had to make do with a couple of torches and whatever food we'd packed.
That sounds grim. Did anyone come to help?
Eventually a Bedouin family spotted our fire and invited us over. It finally dawned on me that we'd been sitting two hundred metres from their camp the whole time!
Ha! So getting stuck was a blessing in disguise, then.
Totally. We stayed up drinking coffee and listening to their stories, and didn't call it a night until well after midnight.

grammar.title: Idioms and Phrasal Verbs in Narrative
grammar.ar: تجعل التعابير الاصطلاحية والأفعال المركّبة (phrasal verbs) السرد طبيعيًا وحيًّا، لكن معناها لا يُستنتج من كلماتها منفردة، لذا يجب حفظها كوحدات كاملة. لاحظ أن بعضها له تركيب ثابت، مثل It dawned on me that حيث يكون الفاعل it أو فكرةً ما، والشخص بعد on. وبعضها يتبعه مفعول بعد حرف الجر مثل make do with something، ولا يجوز فصله.
examples: It suddenly dawned on her that the exam started at eight, not nine.
There was no fridge, so we made do with a cool box full of ice.
Failing the mock exam was a blessing in disguise; it forced me to change my study habits.

words.ex: In layman's terms, a neural network learns by spotting patterns in huge amounts of data.
I'm not sure what you're getting at; could you give me an example?
When the panel looked confused, she calmly rephrased her answer.
The report was so full of jargon that only engineers could follow it.

words.ar: يتلخّص في / يرجع في جوهره إلى
words.ex: The whole debate boils down to one question: who is responsible for the data?
His explanation was so convoluted that I understood less after hearing it.

dialogue.t: Can you help me rehearse? The admissions panel will probably ask me to explain my project on renewable energy storage.
Sure. Pretend I'm your little brother first. What's the project about?
Okay. In layman's terms, solar panels make lots of electricity at noon but none at night, so we need giant 'batteries' to save it for later.
Nice and clear. Now imagine I'm a professor on the panel.

The project evaluates thermal storage as a cost-effective alternative to lithium-ion systems in hot climates. Perhaps I should rephrase that: it compares storing energy as heat with storing it in conventional batteries.
Good, but why does the climate matter?
What I'm getting at is that our extreme heat actually becomes an advantage. To put it another way, the desert isn't just a challenge for engineers; it's a resource.
That's a memorable line. The panel will appreciate that you can adapt your explanation to your audience.

grammar.title: Paraphrase and Clarification Markers
grammar.ar: عند شرح فكرة معقّدة نستخدم عبارات تُنبّه السامع إلى أننا سنعيد الصياغة، مثل To put it another way وPerhaps I should rephrase that. أما What I'm getting at is فهي جملة تأكيدية (pseudo-cleft) تُبرز الفكرة الأساسية في نهاية الجملة. وتشير In layman's terms إلى أننا سنترك المصطلحات التخصصية ونستخدم لغة بسيطة، وهذه مهارة مهمة في المقابلات الجامعية.

The results were statistically insignificant. To put it another way, we can't draw any firm conclusions.

words.ex: With all due respect, I don't think a salary should be the only factor in choosing a career.
I understand where my parents are coming from; they want me to have a secure future.

words.ar: يجرؤ على الاقتراح / يتقدّم برأي بتواضع
words.ex: I'd venture to suggest that passion is just as important as job prospects.
I'll concede that engineering offers more stable employment, but it doesn't suit everyone.
Before deciding, I need to weigh up the pros and cons of each university.
Please don't dismiss graphic design as a hobby; it's a serious profession.

dialogue.t: Your grades are excellent, habibti. Medicine is the obvious choice. It's respected, secure and the family would be proud.
I appreciate where you're coming from, Uncle, yet I'm not sure it's the right fit for me.
Not the right fit? Every student with your marks dreams of becoming a doctor.
With all due respect, I see it slightly differently. I'm genuinely passionate about architecture, and I think I'd excel in it.
But architecture is so unpredictable. Doctors are always needed.
I'll concede that point. But wouldn't it be fair to say that our cities are growing rapidly and need good architects too?
Hmm, perhaps. I just don't want you to regret it later.
I understand, and I value your advice. I'd venture to suggest that I'd be more likely to regret spending seven years on something I don't love.

grammar.title: Softened Contradiction
grammar.ar: في الثقافة العربية لاحترام الكبار مكانة خاصة، وفي الإنجليزية أيضًا يمكنك أن تعارض بأدب باستخدام أدوات تلطيف. نبدأ بالاعتراف بوجهة نظر الآخر (I appreciate where you're coming from)، ثم نخفّف الاعتراض بكلمات مثل slightly وI'd venture to suggest. ويُعدّ السؤال المنفي Wouldn't it be fair to say...? طريقة ذكية لعرض رأيك كأنه أمر يتفق عليه الطرفان بدل أن يكون تحدّيًا مباشرًا.
examples: With all due respect, I see the situation slightly differently.
Wouldn't it be fair to say that job markets change faster than they used to?
I'd venture to suggest that we consider a few alternatives before deciding.

words.ex: I'll begin by outlining the current energy mix in the Gulf before examining its limitations.
Photovoltaic installations in the UAE now produce electricity at a remarkably low cost per kilowatt-hour.
The intermittency of solar power remains a key obstacle, since output drops sharply after sunset.
Renewable energy is increasingly framed as a pillar of economic diversification rather than a purely environmental concern.
The pace of the energy transition will depend as much on policy as on technology.

words.ar: يربط الأفكار المتفرّقة ويجمعها في خلاصة
words.ex: In my final minute, I'll draw the threads together and suggest where the region is heading.

dialogue.t: Good morning, everyone. I'll begin by outlining why the Gulf is uniquely placed to exploit solar energy, before turning to the obstacles that still stand in its way.
That's a clear roadmap. Could you run me through how you'd move from the first section to the second?
Of course. After discussing irradiance levels and falling panel costs, I'd say: this brings me to my second point, namely the problem of intermittency and storage.
Good. And how do you link the obstacles to your proposed solutions without it sounding abrupt?
Having established that storage is the main bottleneck, let us now consider three emerging solutions: battery farms, green hydrogen and regional grid integration.
Excellent. The audience will always know where they are. How do you plan to conclude?
To draw these threads together, I'll argue that the Gulf's challenge is no longer technological but strategic, and then close with a question for the audience.
Ending on a question is a nice touch. Just make sure you pause after each signpost so the structure really registers.

grammar.title: Signposting with gerunds and perfect participle clauses
grammar.ar: تُستخدم عبارات الإرشاد في الخطاب لتوضيح بنية المحاضرة للمستمعين. بعد حروف الجر مثل by وbefore يأتي الفعل بصيغة ‎-ing، مثل: I'll begin by outlining... before turning to.... أما التركيب Having + التصريف الثالث للفعل فيدلّ على أن فكرة قد اكتملت قبل الانتقال إلى الفكرة التالية، ويعادل في العربية «بعد أن أثبتنا...». وانتبه إلى أن فاعل جملة Having established يجب أن يكون هو نفسه فاعل الجملة الرئيسية.
examples: I'll begin by defining what we mean by 'renewable', before turning to the economic case.
Having examined the costs, let us now consider the environmental benefits.
Having outlined the problem, I would now like to propose a possible solution.

words.ex: The first study contends that heavy social media use is a direct cause of anxiety in adolescents.
This finding is corroborated by a large-scale Scandinavian survey conducted over a decade.

words.ar: دراسة طولية (تتبّع المشاركين عبر فترة زمنية)
words.ex: Unlike a snapshot survey, a longitudinal study can reveal how wellbeing changes over time.
Self-reported data on screen time are notoriously unreliable, as teenagers tend to underestimate their usage.
The discrepancy between the two studies may stem from differences in how wellbeing was measured.

words.ar: دقيق ومتعدّد الجوانب / يراعي الفروق الدقيقة
words.ex: A more nuanced picture emerges once we distinguish between passive scrolling and active interaction.

dialogue.t: So, we have two studies that seem to point in completely opposite directions. Where would you start?
Whereas Twenge contends that smartphone use is driving a decline in teenage mental health, Orben and Przybylski maintain that the effect is negligible, roughly comparable to eating potatoes.
Right, but is either position supported elsewhere in the literature?
Twenge's claim about girls in particular is corroborated by several longitudinal datasets. However, Orben's broader conclusion is corroborated by the sheer statistical scale of her analysis.
So how do we reconcile the discrepancy?
The evidence would appear to suggest that the type of use matters more than the amount. Passive scrolling correlates with lower wellbeing, while active messaging does not.
That's a much more nuanced position than either study takes on its own.
Exactly. Taken together, these studies indicate that blanket claims are unhelpful, and that researchers should focus on which teenagers are vulnerable, and why.

grammar.title: Reporting verbs and hedging in synthesis
grammar.ar: عند الجمع بين المصادر نستخدم أفعال نقل دقيقة تعكس موقف الكاتب، مثل contend وmaintain وargue، ولكلّ منها درجة مختلفة من القوة. كما نستخدم أدوات التحفّظ (hedging) مثل would appear to وseem to وindicate بدلاً من prove لتجنّب المبالغة في الاستنتاج، وهذا من سمات الكتابة والحديث الأكاديمي الرصين. ويُستخدم التركيب Whereas X..., Y... للمقارنة بين رأيين متعارضين في جملة واحدة.
examples: Whereas the first author contends that the link is causal, the second maintains that it is merely correlational.
The evidence would appear to suggest that younger users are more susceptible.
Taken together, these findings indicate a modest but measurable effect.

words.ex: The sample is arguably unrepresentative of the wider student population, as it was drawn from a single online university.
Because participation was voluntary, the results may suffer from self-selection bias.
The authors appear to conflate convenience with genuine educational preference.

words.ar: متغيّر مُربِك (يؤثر في النتائج دون أن يُضبط)
words.ex: Household income may be a confounding variable, since wealthier students tend to have better internet access.
A more robust approach would have been to combine questionnaires with classroom observation.

words.ar: يُعمّم / يستقرئ نتائج على نطاق أوسع
words.ex: It would be unwise to extrapolate these findings to secondary schools in the Gulf.

dialogue.t: The headline is striking: seventy-eight percent of students prefer online learning. Are you convinced?
Not entirely. The sample is arguably unrepresentative of students in general. They surveyed people already enrolled on online courses.
Fair point. That's a textbook case of self-selection bias. What else stood out to you?
The whole argument rests on the assumption that preference equals effectiveness. Students might enjoy studying in pyjamas without actually learning more.
And the report claims that students who studied online achieved higher grades because of the format.
Well, correlation should not be conflated with causation. Those students may simply have been more motivated or better resourced to begin with.
So how would you have designed it differently?
A more robust approach would have been to randomly assign students to online and face-to-face groups, and then compare outcomes over a full academic year.

grammar.title: Modal perfects and passive modals for critique
grammar.ar: لنقد منهجية دراسة سابقة نستخدم الأفعال الناقصة مع have والتصريف الثالث للفعل، مثل would have been وshould have + الفعل، للتعبير عمّا كان ينبغي فعله في الماضي ولم يحدث. ويُستخدم المبني للمجهول مع الأفعال الناقصة، مثل should not be conflated، لصياغة قواعد منهجية عامة بأسلوب موضوعي لا يوجّه اللوم إلى شخص بعينه. أما كلمة arguably فتُليّن النقد وتجعله أكثر لباقة أكاديمياً.
examples: A more robust approach would have been to include a control group.
The researchers should have accounted for differences in prior attainment.
Correlation should not be conflated with causation, however compelling the data may seem.

words.ex: Could we perhaps unpack what you mean by 'playing God'?
We seem to have reached a consensus rather quickly, so I'd be interested to hear a dissenting view.

words.ar: تعديل الخلايا التناسلية (تعديل وراثي ينتقل إلى الأجيال اللاحقة)
words.ex: Germline editing raises particular concerns because the changes are inherited by future generations.

words.ar: المنحدر الزلق (حجة أن خطوة صغيرة تقود إلى عواقب خطيرة)
words.ex: Some argue that treating disease today is a slippery slope towards designer babies tomorrow.
Let's not lose sight of the patients for whom this technology could be life-changing.
Please feel free to chime in at any point if you have something to add.

dialogue.t: Thanks, Layla. You suggested that editing embryos to prevent disease is a moral obligation. Could we perhaps unpack that a little further?
Certainly. If we have the means to eliminate conditions like sickle cell anaemia, which is prevalent in parts of our region, then choosing not to act seems ethically questionable.
That's a strong position, and I suspect not everyone shares it. I'd be interested to hear a dissenting view. Omar, you looked sceptical.
Speaking as Omar, I'd say the problem is the slippery slope. Once germline editing is normalised for disease, the line between therapy and enhancement becomes very blurred.
Building on what you said, Omar, who would actually decide where that line is drawn? Governments, doctors, religious scholars?
That's precisely the issue. And there's also the question of access, because only wealthy families might benefit.
Absolutely, but let's not lose sight of our central question, which is whether it's ethical in principle, not just in practice. Would anyone else like to chime in before we move on?

grammar.title: Tentative language for facilitation
grammar.ar: يحتاج مُدير النقاش إلى لغة مهذّبة وغير مباشرة لدعوة المشاركين وتوجيه الحوار دون أن يبدو متسلّطاً. لذلك نستخدم أدوات التلطيف مثل could وperhaps وa little وI'd be interested to... بدلاً من الأوامر المباشرة. ويُستخدم التركيب Let's not + الفعل المجرّد لإعادة النقاش إلى مساره بلطف، أما Building on what you said فيربط مداخلة جديدة بما قاله مشارك سابق، مما يُشعره بالتقدير.
examples: Could we perhaps unpack that assumption a little further?
I'd be interested to hear from someone who hasn't spoken yet.
Let's not lose sight of the original question we set out to answer.

words.ex: The issue of participant attrition is one I've grappled with throughout the design phase.
I'd question the premise that qualitative data are inherently less reliable.
Long-term economic effects lie beyond the scope of this study, but they would merit further research.
I concede that the sample size is modest, but it is appropriate for an exploratory study.
To mitigate researcher bias, two independent coders will analyse the interviews.
The panel was primarily concerned with the methodological rigour of the proposal.

dialogue.t: Your proposal relies on interviewing only twenty students in Riyadh. How can you possibly generalise from that?
That's a fair point, and one I've grappled with. However, the aim isn't statistical generalisation. It's to explore in depth how bilingual students experience academic writing.
But surely without a control group, your findings are essentially anecdotal?

If I understand your question correctly, you're suggesting that only experimental designs produce valid knowledge. I'd question the premise somewhat. Qualitative research has its own criteria for rigour, such as triangulation and member checking.
Very well. And what about the long-term impact on students' university performance?
That lies beyond the scope of this study, but it would be a natural follow-up, perhaps as a longitudinal project tracking the same participants.
And how will you mitigate the risk of your own bias, given that you're a bilingual student yourself?
I concede that my position could influence interpretation, so I'll keep a reflexive journal and have a second researcher independently code a portion of the data.

grammar.title: Concede-and-counter structures with substitution
grammar.ar: عند الردّ على الأسئلة الصعبة، من الأفضل الاعتراف بصحّة جزء من السؤال أولاً ثم تقديم الردّ، وهذا يُسمّى «التسليم ثم الاعتراض». نستخدم كلمة one لتجنّب تكرار الاسم، كما في: That's a fair point, and one I've grappled with، أي «ونقطة تصارعتُ معها». أما If I understand your question correctly فتُستخدم للتأكّد من فهم السؤال وكسب وقت للتفكير، بينما تُليّن كلمة somewhat الاعتراض على الفرضية.
examples: That's a valid concern, and one that several reviewers have raised.
If I understand your question correctly, you're asking whether the results can be replicated.
I'd question the premise somewhat, since the data actually point in the opposite direction.

words.ar: افتراض مخالف للواقع (ماذا لو حدث غير ما حدث)
words.ex: Counterfactual history can illuminate which factors were genuinely decisive.
The printing press transformed European intellectual life within a few generations.
Had printed books been widely available, literacy rates might have risen centuries earlier.
The prestige of the scribal tradition partly explains the slow adoption of print in the Ottoman world.
Print allowed scientific ideas to be disseminated far more rapidly than handwritten manuscripts.
Much of this speculation hinges on whether rulers would have tolerated the free circulation of ideas.

dialogue.t: Let's speculate. Had the printing press reached Baghdad or Cairo in the fifteenth century, where might the Arab world be now?
Had that happened, Arabic would now be one of the dominant languages of modern science, much as it was during the Golden Age.
Interesting, but were it not for the immense prestige of calligraphy and the scribal tradition, wouldn't print have been adopted anyway?
Possibly, though the technical difficulty of printing connected Arabic script was a genuine barrier. Supposing that it had been overcome early, what would follow?
I'd imagine much higher literacy rates and a far more rapid dissemination of translated works, perhaps even an Arab scientific revolution running parallel to Europe's.
Mind you, it hinges on political will. But for state control over what was printed, Europe's Reformation might never have happened either.
True. Were Arab rulers to have embraced print enthusiastically, the balance of intellectual power could look very different today.
Of course, counterfactuals can never be proven, but they force us to think hard about cause and effect.

grammar.title: Mixed and inverted conditionals
grammar.ar: الجملة الشرطية المختلطة تربط شرطاً في الماضي بنتيجة في الحاضر، مثل: Had X happened, Y would now be... أي «لو حدث كذا في الماضي لكان كذا الآن». وفي الأسلوب الرسمي نحذف if ونقدّم الفعل المساعد على الفاعل، فتصبح If it had happened هي Had it happened. أما Were it not for وBut for فيُعادلان «لولا» في العربية ويأتي بعدهما اسم لا جملة. ويُستخدم Supposing that لطرح فرضية ثم مناقشة نتائجها.
examples: Had the printing press arrived earlier, the region would now have a far richer archive of printed texts.
Were it not for the translation movement, much Greek philosophy would have been lost.
But for the invention of movable type, the Renaissance might have unfolded very differently.

words.ar: ثلاثية بلاغية (تتابع ثلاث كلمات أو عبارات متوازية)
words.ex: Her closing tricolon, 'We must imagine, innovate and invest', drew thunderous applause from the forum.

words.ar: التكرار الاستهلالي (تكرار كلمة أو عبارة في بداية جمل متتالية)
words.ex: By repeating 'We are the generation that...' at the start of each line, the speaker used anaphora to build momentum.

words.ar: المقابلة أو الطباق (الجمع بين فكرتين متضادتين في بناء متوازٍ)
words.ex: The antithesis 'not a burden but an opportunity' reframed the whole debate on youth employment.
A well-crafted speech can galvanise an apathetic audience into genuine civic engagement.

words.ar: نداء مدوٍّ أو دعوة حاسمة إلى التحرك
words.ex: Vision 2030 is nothing less than a clarion call to every young Saudi to shape the nation's future.
Personal anecdotes tend to resonate with young audiences far more than abstract statistics.

dialogue.t: I've drafted my opening for the youth forum, but it feels rather flat. It just lists what Vision 2030 offers.
Then why not open with a rhetorical question? Something like, 'Can we truly afford to wait while the world races ahead?'
That's sharper. I also want to challenge the idea that young people are a strain on the economy.
An antithesis would land perfectly there: 'Our youth is not a burden but an opportunity, not a cost but an investment.'
And for the climax, I was thinking of a tricolon: 'We must imagine, innovate and invest.'
Excellent. Reinforce it with anaphora as well: 'We are the generation that builds. We are the generation that leads. We are the generation that delivers.'
Isn't that overdoing it, though? I don't want to sound theatrical.
Not if you use them sparingly. One device per section is enough to galvanise the audience without exhausting them.

grammar.title: Rhetorical Structures for Impact
grammar.ar: تعتمد الخطابة المؤثرة على البنى المتوازية: الثلاثية (tricolon) تجمع ثلاثة أفعال أو أسماء من النوع النحوي نفسه، مثل imagine, innovate and invest. أما المقابلة (antithesis) فتضع فكرتين متضادتين في قالب متوازٍ باستخدام not X but Y. والتكرار الاستهلالي (anaphora) يكرر العبارة نفسها في بداية الجمل، وهو مألوف في الخطابة العربية، لكن الإنجليزية تتطلب الحفاظ على التوازي النحوي الدقيق. أما السؤال البلاغي فلا ينتظر جواباً، بل يُستخدم لإشراك الجمهور وتأكيد فكرة.
examples: We must imagine boldly, innovate relentlessly and invest wisely.
Change is not a threat to our identity but an expression of it.
If not us, then who? If not now, then when? Can we truly afford to wait?

words.ar: الثقافة المالية (القدرة على فهم المال وإدارته)
words.ex: Without financial literacy, young adults are easy prey for high-interest credit schemes.
Making personal finance a compulsory subject would ensure that no student graduates unprepared.
Budgeting is an indispensable life skill, yet it is rarely taught in a structured way.
Predatory lending thrives precisely where consumers fail to understand interest rates.
Recent surveys underscore the alarming gap between teenagers' spending habits and their financial knowledge.
It is precisely this lack of awareness that leaves so many graduates in debt.

dialogue.t: I'm arguing that financial literacy should be compulsory, but my points keep blending together.
You need emphatic syntax. Try opening with inversion: 'Never before has it been so crucial to understand money.'
Good. Then I could add, 'Not only does it protect students from debt, but it also prepares them to invest.'
Exactly. And what's the core issue for you personally?
What concerns me most is that teenagers can now borrow online with a single tap.
Then hammer that home with a cleft: 'It is precisely this ease of access that makes education indispensable.'
Only by structuring it like this will the panel see which points really matter.
Just don't use inversion in every sentence, or it'll sound contrived rather than compelling.

grammar.title: Emphasis: Negative Inversion and Cleft Sentences
grammar.ar: عندما تبدأ الجملة بظرف نفي أو تقييد مثل Never before أو Not only أو Only by، يجب قلب ترتيب الفاعل والفعل المساعد، فنقول Not only does it… لا Not only it does…. وإذا لم يوجد فعل مساعد نستخدم do/does/did. أما جمل التبئير (cleft sentences) مثل What concerns me most is… و It is precisely this that… فتفصل الجملة إلى جزأين لتسليط الضوء على عنصر واحد. ينبغي لمتعلمي العربية الانتباه إلى أن هذا القلب إلزامي في الإنجليزية وليس اختيارياً كما في العربية.
examples: Never before has it been so crucial to teach young people how to manage their money.
Not only does financial education reduce debt, but it also fosters long-term independence.
What concerns me most is how easily students can access credit; it is precisely this that schools must address.

words.ex: The motion before us today is that university education should be free for all.
The proposition must establish a clear and consistent case from the very first speech.
Our second pillar concerns the long-term economic return on an educated population.
As the side proposing change, we accept that the burden of proof lies with us.
Free tuition is one of the most powerful levers of socio-economic mobility.
A true meritocracy rewards talent, not the size of a family's bank account.

dialogue.t: Madam Speaker, we on the proposition side firmly believe that university education should be free for all.
Point of information: does 'free' mean the state pays for everything, including accommodation?
A fair question, which brings me neatly to my next step. Let me define the terms of this debate: by 'free', we mean tuition fees fully funded by the state.
Thank you. And on what grounds do you justify such enormous public expenditure?
Our case rests on three pillars: equality of opportunity, economic return, and social cohesion.
Yet surely those who benefit most should contribute something?
They do, through higher taxes over a lifetime. I urge the house to consider the cost of the talent we lose when bright students cannot afford to enrol.
We'll address that in our rebuttal, but your framing is certainly clear.

grammar.title: Formal Debate Conventions and Signposting
grammar.ar: تتبع المناظرات الرسمية صيغاً ثابتة: يُخاطب المتحدث رئيس الجلسة (Madam Speaker / Mr Speaker) ويشير إلى الجمهور بـ the house. نستخدم عبارات التوجيه (signposting) مثل Our case rests on… و Let me define… لتنظيم الحجج. لاحظ أن الفعل urge يتبعه مفعول به ثم to + المصدر (I urge the house to consider)، بينما consider يتبعه اسم أو فعل بصيغة ing-. وتُستخدم We firmly believe بدلاً من We think لإظهار الثقة والرسمية.
examples: We on the proposition side firmly believe that access to education is a right, not a privilege.
Let me define the terms of this debate before turning to our three pillars.
I urge the house to consider what is lost when talent is filtered by wealth.

words.ex: The second speaker's role is to rebut the opposition's strongest claim before introducing new material.

words.ar: يُسلّم بـ أو يعترف بصحة نقطة
words.ex: Skilled debaters concede minor points in order to strengthen their credibility on major ones.
The claim that smartphones improve concentration simply does not hold water.

words.ar: استنتاج لا يترتب منطقياً على مقدماته
words.ex: Arguing that phones must be banned because some students cheat is a classic non sequitur.

words.ar: مغالطة رجل القش (تحريف حجة الخصم لتسهيل مهاجمتها)
words.ex: My opponent has attacked a straw man; we never argued for unrestricted phone use.
Saying that all teenagers are addicted to their screens is a sweeping generalisation.

dialogue.t: My opponent claims that smartphones are essential learning tools, yet this overlooks the overwhelming evidence on distraction.
The evidence is mixed. Many students use their phones for research and translation.
Even if we were to concede that some students use them productively, it still does not follow that the benefits outweigh the harm for the majority.
But banning them treats every student as irresponsible. Isn't that a sweeping generalisation?
On the contrary, a ban protects responsible students from the constant interruptions caused by others.
Schools could simply teach digital self-discipline instead.
In theory, perhaps, but that argument simply does not hold water when teachers already struggle to cover the curriculum.
Then we fundamentally disagree on whether the solution is restriction or education.

grammar.title: Concessive Conditionals for Rebuttal
grammar.ar: تُستخدم صيغة Even if we were to + المصدر لافتراض صحة حجة الخصم مؤقتاً ثم إثبات أن النتيجة لا تتغير، وتكملها عادة عبارة it still does not follow that. تفيد were to أن الافتراض بعيد أو نظري. أما On the contrary فتستخدم فقط لرفض فكرة وإثبات عكسها، ولا تعني on the other hand التي تضيف وجهة نظر مقابلة دون رفض، وهو خلط شائع لدى المتعلمين العرب.
examples: Even if we were to concede that phones aid research, it still does not follow that they belong in every lesson.
My opponent claims that bans are outdated, yet this overlooks recent studies on attention spans.
Banning phones does not limit learning; on the contrary, it restores focus to the classroom.

words.ar: مقايضة أو موازنة بين مكسبين متعارضين
words.ex: Every mega-project involves a trade-off between rapid development and ecological preservation.
At stake here is not merely a coastline but an entire marine ecosystem.

words.ar: لا رجعة فيه، لا يمكن إصلاحه
words.ex: Some environmental damage is irreversible, no matter how much is later invested in restoration.

words.ar: الإشراف المسؤول والأمانة في رعاية الموارد
words.ex: Environmental stewardship requires us to see ourselves as custodians rather than owners of the land.
Intergenerational equity demands that we do not exhaust resources our grandchildren will need.
Developers have pledged to mitigate the impact on migratory birds through protected corridors.

dialogue.t: Mega-projects create jobs and diversify the economy. Surely that justifies some environmental cost?
It is a question of striking a balance between prosperity today and sustainability tomorrow.
Agreed, but delaying development indefinitely carries its own risks.
Of course. Yet at stake here is a fragile coral reef that, once destroyed, cannot be rebuilt.
One cannot reasonably justify halting national progress for a single reef, however valuable it may be.
Nor can one justify irreversible damage simply because the economic gains are tempting. The ends do not necessarily justify the means.
So what would you propose instead?
Rigorous impact assessments and genuine stewardship, so that we mitigate harm rather than merely compensate for it afterwards.

grammar.title: Fronting and Impersonal 'One' for Weighing Values
grammar.ar: في عبارة At stake here is… نقدّم الخبر إلى بداية الجملة (fronting) ويأتي الفعل قبل الفاعل، لإبراز ما هو مهدد بالخطر. ويُستخدم الضمير غير الشخصي one في الكتابة والخطاب الرسمي للتعبير عن حكم عام موضوعي بدلاً من you، مثل One cannot reasonably justify…. وتأتي however هنا بمعنى 'مهما' عندما يتبعها صفة أو ظرف (however valuable). وتُستعمل Nor + فعل مساعد + فاعل لإضافة نفي ثانٍ مع القلب.
examples: At stake here is the survival of species found nowhere else on earth.
One cannot reasonably justify such destruction, however profitable the project may be.
It is a question of striking a balance between ambition and responsibility, for the ends do not necessarily justify the means.

words.ex: A common misconception is that Saudi society has remained unchanged for decades.
Personal stories are often more effective than statistics in dispelling stereotypes.
Many visitors arrive with preconceived notions that rarely survive their first week.
A nuanced presentation acknowledges complexity rather than offering a polished advertisement.
Saudi hospitality, expressed through coffee and dates, is a cornerstone of social life.
Addressing stereotypes requires tact; lecturing an audience will only make them defensive.

dialogue.t: I'm presenting Saudi heritage to the exchange students, but I'm worried about sounding defensive.
Then avoid saying 'You're wrong'. Try 'Allow me to offer a different perspective' instead.
Good. I'd like to start with hospitality, since many of them see it as a mere formality.
You could say, 'Far from being a mere formality, Arabic coffee is in fact a gesture of trust and respect.'
And then tackle the idea that the culture is static: 'Contrary to popular perception, Saudi society is evolving rapidly.'
Just be nuanced. Acknowledge what's changing without dismissing the traditions people value.
Right. Perhaps I'll add, 'It is often overlooked that heritage and modernity coexist here quite naturally.'
Perfect. That kind of tact will dispel stereotypes far more effectively than any argument.

grammar.title: Contrastive Framing: 'Far from being...'
grammar.ar: تُستخدم Far from + اسم أو فعل بصيغة ing- أو being + صفة لنفي تصور شائع ثم تقديم الحقيقة البديلة، وغالباً ما تتبعها it is in fact. وتُقدّم Contrary to popular perception و It is often overlooked that تصحيحاً مهذباً دون مهاجمة الجمهور. هذه العبارات أكثر لباقة من النفي المباشر، وهي مهمة في التواصل بين الثقافات. انتبه إلى أن ما بعد Far from يكون اسماً أو صيغة ing- ولا يأتي بعده فعل مصرّف.
examples: Far from being a rigid tradition, Saudi hospitality is in fact a living, adaptable practice.
Contrary to popular perception, young Saudis are deeply engaged with global culture.
It is often overlooked that the Arabian Peninsula was a crossroads of trade for millennia.

words.ar: مختلف تمامًا عن / بعيد كل البعد عن
words.ex: My hometown today is a far cry from the quiet fishing village my grandparents grew up in.
In my final year, I've started to gravitate towards subjects that combine logic with creativity.

words.ar: مُشبَع بـ / غارق في (تاريخ أو تقاليد)
words.ex: The old quarter of the city is steeped in history, with souqs dating back centuries.
After a demanding week of revision, I unwind by sketching on the rooftop.
It's a bustling coastal city, especially during the summer months.
I'm hoping to pursue architecture at university, provided my grades hold up.

dialogue.t: Let's talk about your hometown. What do you like most about it?
I'd have to say it's the waterfront. The city has become quite bustling, but the corniche still has a calm about it, particularly in the early evening.
Are you studying or working at the moment?
I'm in my final year of secondary school. Truth be told, it's been more intense than I anticipated, though I'm learning to pace myself.
Do you have any hobbies?

Well, it's not so much a hobby as a way of switching off. I do calligraphy. These days I find myself increasingly drawn to the more experimental styles, which are a far cry from what I was taught as a child.
Has that changed since you were younger?
Quite a bit. I used to see it as a chore, whereas now I genuinely gravitate towards it whenever I need to unwind.

grammar.title: Contrastive focus: 'It's not so much X as Y'
grammar.ar: يُستخدم التركيب 'It's not so much X as Y' لتصحيح وصفٍ أو تدقيقه، فالمعنى: الأمر ليس X بقدر ما هو Y. يجب أن يكون X وY من النوع النحوي نفسه (اسمان أو صفتان أو فعلان). أما 'I find myself + V-ing' فيعبّر عن تغيّر تلقائي غير مخطَّط له في السلوك، وهو أكثر طبيعية من 'I started to'. انتبه: لا تقل 'not so much X than Y'، فالصحيح 'as'.
examples: It's not so much the weather I miss as the sense of community.
For me, reading is not so much a pastime as a necessity.
These days I find myself spending far less time on social media.

words.ex: Meeting her proved to be a pivotal moment in how I viewed my own abilities.

words.ar: عند النظر إلى الماضي / بأثر رجعي
words.ex: In hindsight, his criticism was the most generous thing anyone did for me that year.
Volunteering abroad broadened my horizons in ways no classroom could.

words.ar: متواضع / لا يلفت الانتباه إلى نفسه
words.ex: He was an unassuming man, yet everyone in the room listened when he spoke.
My chemistry teacher instilled in me a genuine curiosity about the world.

words.ar: المرونة والقدرة على التعافي من الصعاب
words.ex: What she taught me, above all, was resilience in the face of failure.

dialogue.t: I'd like you to describe a person who changed your perspective. You have one minute to prepare.
The person I'd like to talk about is my former physics teacher, Mr Haddad, a rather unassuming man who joined our school when I was fifteen.
What struck me most was that he never gave us the answer. He'd simply ask another question until we worked it out ourselves, which, at the time, I found utterly infuriating.
Little did I know that this habit would completely reshape the way I approach problems, not only in science but in everyday life.
It was only later, when I faced a genuinely difficult exam, that it occurred to me he'd been training us to tolerate uncertainty rather than fear it.
Looking back, I realise he instilled in me a kind of intellectual resilience. It was a pivotal year, and in hindsight, I owe him a great deal.
Thank you. Do you still keep in touch with him?
Occasionally, yes. I sent him a message when I got my results, and I think he was quietly proud.

grammar.title: Negative inversion and 'It was only later that...'
grammar.ar: بعد العبارات السلبية أو المقيِّدة مثل 'Little' و'Never' و'Only later' في بداية الجملة، نقلب ترتيب الفاعل والفعل المساعد كما في السؤال: 'Little did I know' وليس 'Little I knew'. أما تركيب 'It was only later that + جملة' فهو جملة مُشطورة (cleft) تُبرز توقيت الإدراك. يضيف هذان التركيبان طابعًا سرديًا دراميًا، ويرفعان تقييم المدى النحوي في IELTS.
examples: Little did I realise how much that conversation would matter.
Only later did I understand why she had been so strict with us.
It was only when I left home that I appreciated my parents' sacrifices.

words.ex: Rapid urbanisation has exacerbated pressure on housing and public transport.
Urban sprawl often leaves residents entirely dependent on private cars.
Automation is likely to transform rather than simply eliminate many jobs.
Governments must plan for job displacement caused by artificial intelligence.
We are living through a period of unprecedented technological change.
Access to technology still depends heavily on socio-economic background.

dialogue.t: Why do you think so many young people are moving to large cities?
This could be attributed to a number of factors, chiefly the concentration of universities and employment, but also the perception that cities offer greater personal freedom.
Is that a positive development?
On an individual level, often yes. On a broader societal level, however, it can exacerbate urban sprawl and leave rural areas economically hollowed out.
How might technology change the way people work in the future?
There's a growing tendency for companies to adopt remote and hybrid models, which could, paradoxically, reverse some of that migration to cities.
So will automation be beneficial overall?
It largely hinges on how the transition is managed. Without retraining schemes, job displacement could deepen existing socio-economic divides on an unprecedented scale.

grammar.title: Impersonal and passive structures for analysis
grammar.ar: في المناقشة المجردة نستخدم تراكيب غير شخصية مثل 'This could be attributed to' و'It largely hinges on' و'There's a growing tendency for + اسم + to-infinitive' لتقديم الأفكار بموضوعية بدلًا من 'I think' المتكررة. لاحظ أن 'attribute' يأتي مع حرف الجر 'to'، و'hinge' يأتي مع 'on'. كذلك تُسهم الأسماء المشتقة (nominalisation) مثل 'the concentration of' في جعل الأسلوب أكثر أكاديمية.
examples: The decline in reading could partly be attributed to the rise of short-form video.
Whether remote work succeeds largely hinges on trust between employers and staff.
There's a growing tendency for young professionals to change careers several times.

words.ar: تكون له الأولوية / يتقدّم على غيره
words.ex: Safety should surely take precedence over aesthetics.
There's an inevitable trade-off between cost and long-term impact.
We should consider the feasibility of each proposal within a limited budget.
The council could allocate more funding to green spaces.
After some debate, we managed to reach a consensus on the top priority.

words.ar: يحوّل منطقة إلى منطقة مخصّصة للمشاة
words.ex: Pedestrianising the old market would make it far more welcoming.

dialogue.t: Shall we start with public transport? It seems to affect the greatest number of residents.
I can see the merit in that, though I'd argue that air quality is more urgent, given how many people suffer from respiratory problems.
That's a fair point. But wouldn't better transport actually reduce pollution in the long run?
True, but the feasibility is questionable. A new metro line would take a decade, whereas planting trees and pedestrianising the centre could happen within a year.
Would you agree that quick, visible improvements take precedence if we want the campaign to gain public support?
Absolutely, as long as we don't lose sight of the bigger picture. It's a trade-off, really.
So, are we in agreement that green spaces come first, with transport as a close second?
Yes, I think we've reached a consensus. Housing can go third, since it requires the most funding to be allocated.

grammar.title: Tentative language for negotiation
grammar.ar: في المهمة التعاونية يقيّم الممتحِن قدرتك على التفاوض لا على الفوز في الجدال. لذلك نستخدم أسئلة نفي ومقترحات مهذّبة مثل 'Shall we...?' و'Wouldn't...?' و'Would you agree that...?' لدعوة الشريك إلى المشاركة. وللاعتراض بلطف نعترف أولًا بقيمة رأيه ثم نضيف تحفّظنا: 'I can see the merit in that, though...'. تجنّب العبارات المباشرة الحادة مثل 'You're wrong'.
examples: Wouldn't it make more sense to focus on young people first?
I take your point, though I'm not entirely convinced it's the most cost-effective option.
Would you agree that education should take precedence over infrastructure?

words.ex: I would contend that tradition gives communities a sense of continuity.
Globalisation is gradually eroding regional dialects.
Museums play a vital role in safeguarding intangible heritage.
Preserving cultural heritage need not mean rejecting modern life.
The relationship between progress and tradition is far more nuanced than it first appears.
Some customs become obsolete simply because the conditions that created them disappear.

dialogue.t: Your question is: 'Is progress always at the expense of tradition?' Please speak for about two minutes.
This raises the question of whether progress and tradition are genuinely in opposition, or whether we simply perceive them that way.
There are compelling arguments on both sides. Rapid modernisation has undoubtedly eroded certain crafts and dialects, yet technology has also allowed us to record and safeguard them as never before.
Ultimately, I would contend that the relationship is far more nuanced than a simple trade-off. Traditions that remain meaningful tend to adapt rather than disappear.
But aren't some traditions simply obsolete? Should we preserve them at all?
That's a fair challenge. Certain practices certainly have outlived their purpose. That said, I wouldn't go so far as to claim that we should abandon anything that lacks an obvious function.
Why not?
Because much of our cultural heritage is symbolic. Its value lies in the sense of identity it provides, not in its practicality.

grammar.title: Hedging and concession in extended argument
grammar.ar: في الحديث المطوّل بمستوى C2 لا نعرض الرأي بشكل مطلق، بل نوازن بين المواقف ثم نحدّد موقفنا بحذر. تُستخدم 'That said,' للتراجع الجزئي بعد عرض فكرة، و'I wouldn't go so far as to + فعل' لرفض الموقف المتطرف. أما 'I would contend that' فتقدّم استنتاجًا قويًا بأسلوب رسمي، ويخفّف الفعل الشرطي 'would' من حدّته.
examples: Social media has clear drawbacks. That said, it has given a voice to many marginalised groups.
I wouldn't go so far as to say that all modern architecture lacks character.
Ultimately, I would contend that education is the most effective way to preserve tradition.

words.ex: Water scarcity is a pressing concern across much of the region.
Artificial intelligence will have far-reaching implications for education.
Saying all teenagers are addicted to their phones is a sweeping generalisation.
Many hospitals are facing an acute shortage of qualified nurses.
Solar power has become a viable alternative to fossil fuels.
I said 'decrease', but that was a slip of the tongue. I meant 'increase'.

dialogue.t: What do you see as the biggest challenge facing your country in the coming decades?
I'd say water scarcity is the most pressing concern, or rather, the way we manage the water we already have.
Why the management rather than the scarcity itself?
Because agriculture uses a vast amount and much of it is wasted. Let me put that more accurately: inefficient irrigation accounts for a significant proportion of the losses.
And what could be done about it?
There's a technique, the word escapes me, but it's a kind of system where water is delivered drop by drop directly to the roots.
Drip irrigation?

Exactly, drip irrigation. It's a viable alternative, and if adopted widely, it would have far-reaching implications. What I mean to say is that it could transform food security, not merely save water.

grammar.title: Reformulation and recovery strategies
grammar.ar: التصحيح الذاتي ليس نقطة ضعف؛ بل يرفع التقييم إذا جاء بسلاسة ودقة، لأنه يُظهر وعيك اللغوي. استخدم 'or rather' لتصحيح كلمة فورًا، و'Let me put that more accurately' أو 'What I mean to say is' لإعادة صياغة فكرة كاملة. وعندما تنسى كلمة، لا تتوقف ولا تنتقل إلى العربية، بل صِفها بعبارة 'The word escapes me, but it's a kind of...' (أسلوب الالتفاف حول الكلمة) لتحافظ على الطلاقة.
examples: The policy was introduced in 2015, or rather, it was announced then and implemented two years later.
It's bad for the environment. Let me put that more accurately: it significantly increases carbon emissions.
The word escapes me, but it's a kind of tool used to measure air pressure.

units.cando: Can convey finer shades of meaning precisely by using a wide range of qualifying devices, and can understand and respond to implicit attitudes, irony and understatement with ease.
lessons: Hedging and Degrees of Certainty
Discuss whether AI will replace human translators, calibrating claims from tentative speculation to firm conviction
Graded modality and hedging with 'It would be premature to suggest that...', 'There is a strong case to be made that...', 'I'm inclined to think..., albeit with reservations', 'In all likelihood...'
Reading Between the Lines
Interpret what a speaker really means in ambiguous family, school or workplace exchanges and respond tactfully
Inferring and voicing implicature with 'What she seems to be implying is...', 'Reading between the lines, ...', 'I take it you're not entirely convinced?', 'That's not to say that...'
Irony, Understatement and Tone
Analyse sarcasm and understatement in a viral social media post and discuss how tone shifts meaning
Understatement and ironic framing with 'It wasn't exactly a triumph', 'That's putting it mildly', 'One might be forgiven for thinking...', 'Not the most tactful remark, to say the least'
Idiomatic and Colloquial Fluency
Retell a stressful exam week or a desert camping trip to a friend using natural, idiomatic English
Idioms and phrasal verbs in context with 'I was at my wits' end', 'It turned out to be a blessing in disguise', 'We had to make do with...', 'It finally dawned on me that...'
Reformulating and Clarifying
Rephrase a complex idea for different listeners, such as a younger sibling, a teacher or a university admissions panel
Paraphrase and clarification with 'To put it another way...', 'What I'm getting at is...', 'In layman's terms...', 'Perhaps I should rephrase that: ...'
Diplomatic Disagreement
Respectfully challenge an elder's or a mentor's view on choosing a university major without causing offence
Softened contradiction with 'With all due respect, I see it slightly differently', 'I appreciate where you're coming from, yet...', 'Wouldn't it be fair to say that...?', 'I'd venture to suggest...'

units.cando: Can present a complex academic topic fluently and authoritatively to a critical audience, structure it logically, and handle difficult or hostile questioning with precision.
lessons: Structuring an Academic Talk
Deliver a five-minute mini-lecture on renewable energy in the Gulf with a clear signposted structure

Discourse signposting with 'I'll begin by outlining..., before turning to...', 'This brings me to my second point', 'Having established that..., let us now consider...', 'To draw these threads together...'
Synthesising Sources
Compare two conflicting studies on social media and teenage wellbeing and draw a balanced conclusion
Citing and synthesising with 'Whereas X contends that..., Y maintains...', 'This finding is corroborated by...', 'The evidence would appear to suggest...', 'Taken together, these studies indicate...'
Critiquing Methodology and Evidence
Evaluate the strengths and flaws of a survey claiming most students prefer online learning

Critical evaluation with 'The sample is arguably unrepresentative of...', 'This rests on the assumption that...', 'Correlation should not be conflated with causation', 'A more robust approach would have been to...'
Leading a Seminar Discussion
Facilitate a peer discussion on the ethics of gene editing, inviting contributions and managing turn-taking
Facilitation language with 'Could we perhaps unpack that a little further?', 'I'd be interested to hear a dissenting view', 'Let's not lose sight of...', 'Building on what you said...'
Handling Challenging Questions
Defend a research proposal under tough questioning from a simulated university panel

Fielding questions with 'That's a fair point, and one I've grappled with', 'If I understand your question correctly...', 'I'd question the premise somewhat', 'That lies beyond the scope of this study, but...'
Abstract and Hypothetical Reasoning
Speculate on how history might have unfolded had the printing press reached the Arab world earlier
Mixed and inverted conditionals with 'Had X happened, Y would now be...', 'Were it not for..., ...', 'Supposing that..., what would follow?', 'But for this development, ...'

units.cando: Can argue a case persuasively on complex and contentious issues, using rhetorical devices and emphasis effectively, and can rebut opposing arguments convincingly and spontaneously.
lessons: Rhetorical Devices for Impact
Craft a persuasive speech for a youth forum on the role of young Saudis in Vision 2030
Rhetorical structures with tricolon 'We must imagine, innovate and invest', rhetorical questions 'Can we truly afford to wait?', antithesis 'not a burden but an opportunity', and anaphora
Emphasis Through Inversion and Clefting
Highlight the most important points when arguing for compulsory financial literacy in schools
Emphatic syntax with 'Never before has it been so crucial to...', 'Not only does it..., but it also...', 'What concerns me most is...', 'It is precisely this that...'
Formal Debate: Opening Arguments
Propose the motion 'This house believes that university education should be free for all' in a structured debate
Debate conventions with 'We on the proposition side firmly believe...', 'Our case rests on three pillars', 'Let me define the terms of this debate', 'I urge the house to consider...'
Rebuttal and Counter-Argument
Dismantle the opposition's case on banning smartphones in classrooms point by point

Rebuttal language with 'My opponent claims..., yet this overlooks...', 'This argument simply does not hold water', 'Even if we were to concede that..., it still does not follow that...', 'On the contrary...'
Ethical Dilemmas and Values
Debate the balance between economic growth and environmental conservation in mega-projects
Weighing values with 'It is a question of striking a balance between...', 'At stake here is...', 'One cannot reasonably justify..., however...', 'The ends do not necessarily justify the means'
Cross-Cultural Persuasion
Present Saudi heritage and hospitality to an international student audience, addressing stereotypes with tact
Audience-aware persuasion with 'Contrary to popular perception...', 'Allow me to offer a different perspective', 'It is often overlooked that...', 'Far from being..., it is in fact...'

units.t: Exam Mastery: C2 Proficiency and IELTS Band 9
units.ar: إتقان الاختبارات: كفاءة C2 والدرجة 9 في آيلتس
units.cando: Can perform with complete fluency, accuracy and flexibility in timed exam speaking tasks, sustaining extended, well-organised responses on abstract topics with native-like ease.
lessons: IELTS Part 1: Natural Elaboration
Answer personal questions on hometown, studies and hobbies with spontaneous, sophisticated extension
Natural extension with 'I'd have to say...', 'Truth be told, ...', 'It's not so much X as Y', 'These days I find myself increasingly drawn to...'
IELTS Part 2: The Two-Minute Long Turn
Deliver a cohesive two-minute talk on a person who changed your perspective, after one minute of preparation
Narrative cohesion with 'What struck me most was...', 'Little did I know that...', 'Looking back, I realise...', 'It was only later that it occurred to me...'
IELTS Part 3: Abstract Discussion
Discuss societal questions on technology, urbanisation and the future of work at band 9 depth
Abstract analysis with 'This could be attributed to a number of factors...', 'On a broader societal level...', 'There's a growing tendency for...', 'It largely hinges on...'
C2 Proficiency: Collaborative Task
Negotiate with a partner to rank priorities for a city improvement campaign, reaching a reasoned decision
Collaborative negotiation with 'Shall we start with...?', 'I can see the merit in that, though...', 'Would you agree that... takes precedence?', 'So, are we in agreement that...?'
C2 Proficiency: Long Turn with Follow-Up
Speak at length on a prompt card about progress and tradition, then respond to the examiner's probing questions

Extended argument with 'This raises the question of whether...', 'There are compelling arguments on both sides', 'Ultimately, I would contend that...', 'That said, I wouldn't go so far as to claim...'
Self-Correction and Lexical Range Under Pressure
Complete a full mock speaking exam with feedback on accuracy, range and recovery strategies

Recovery and precision with 'or rather...', 'Let me put that more accurately', 'What I mean to say is...', 'The word escapes me, but it's a kind of...', plus less common collocations such as 'a pressing concern' and 'far-reaching implications'
